violation: The operator key registry (GOBLIN-DIV-015 piece 1) is unforgeable through the Raft log and forgeable through a snapshot. Every guard - the empty-registry seed rule, the last-key refusal, the prev_serial replay guard, signature verification against replicated key material - runs inside FSM Apply. InstallSnapshot does not go through Apply. FSM.Restore installs payload.GetOperatorKeys() directly, and a snapshot is not a signed object. An attacker able to append arbitrary Raft log entries can by construction act as leader on the raft-quic plane, forge an FSMSnapshot whose operator_keys map holds their own well-formed key, and install it as the cluster's root of trust on every replica in one step. This falsifies the rationale the piece-1 plan gives for the last-key rule ('if any node in the Raft membership could empty and re-seed the registry, node compromise would become operator compromise') - node compromise does become operator compromise, through the snapshot door rather than the log door. Restore now validates each record's derived key id and refuses a mismatch, which makes the id-is-derived invariant hold off the Apply path too, but no check inside Restore can distinguish an honest leader's snapshot from a hostile peer's. Found by the piece-1 whole-branch review 2026-07-30; every per-task review before it asked whether the log door could be forced and none asked whether the log was the only door.

(1) resolveOperatorKey takes no lock at all. It is safe today only because its single non-test caller is applyOperatorKeyChange, which runs under Apply's write lock; any read-path caller races Apply. Its doc says 'callers hold f.mu', which reads as a note rather than the load-bearing constraint it is. The seeder's drift check is advisory and non-fatal by design. A consumer that fails OPEN on staleness inverts this silently, and piece 2's mint RPC is exactly that consumer: a follower that has not yet applied an OPERATOR_KEY_CHANGE remove still resolves the removed key and would mint a capability token for a revoked operator. That is a revocation bypass on the piece whose entire purpose is revocation, reached without any attacker capability beyond asking a lagging replica.
